source: To specifically label PCDH15 subunits with single gold particles, we developed a high affinity, low off-rate (koff=4.6×10–5 1 /s), anti-PCDH15 monoclonal antibody (mAb), termed 39G7.
evidence: This describes a reagent developed in the study.

claim: The 39G7 mAb has a koff of 4.6×10–5 1/s.
source: To specifically label PCDH15 subunits with single gold particles, we developed a high affinity, low off-rate (koff=4.6×10–5 1 /s), anti-PCDH15 monoclonal antibody (mAb), termed 39G7.
evidence: This is a measured property of the 39G7 antibody.

claim: The 39G7 mAb binds to the EC3 cadherin repeat of PCDH15.
source: By examining the binding of 39G7 to a series of PCDH15 truncation constructs, we determined that the mAb binds to the EC3 cadherin repeat, near the amino terminus (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from binding studies supported by Figure 2A.

claim: The 39G7 mAb stained PCDH15 on the surface of vestibular stereocilia in the presence or absence of calcium.
source: Similar to the anti-PCDH15 pAbs, the 39G7 mAb stained PCDH15 on the surface of vestibular stereocilia, either in the presence or absence of calcium (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by Figure 2B.

claim: A 39G7 Fab construct with a single free cysteine residue at the C terminus of the heavy chain was created.
source: To create a reagent to label PCDH15 subunits with a single gold particle, we created a 39G7 Fab construct with a single free cysteine residue at the C terminus of the heavy chain, thus enabling conjugation of the Fab to 3 nm AuNPs (Azubel et al., 2019, p. 2).
evidence: This describes a reagent engineering step performed in the study.

claim: Purification of the 39G7 Fab – AuNP complex via polyacrylamide electrophoresis and size exclusion chromatography yielded a homogeneous species in which the Fab was labeled with a single AuNP.
source: Purification of the 39G7 Fab – AuNP complex via polyacrylamide electrophoresis and size exclusion chromatography (SEC) yielded a homogeneous species in which the Fab was a labeled with a single AuNP (Figure 2C+D), devoid of non-AuNP-labeled Fabs.
evidence: This is a primary experimental result supported by Figures 2C and 2D.

claim: The purified 39G7 Fab-AuNP reagent was devoid of non-AuNP-labeled Fabs.
source: Purification of the 39G7 Fab – AuNP complex via polyacrylamide electrophoresis and size exclusion chromatography (SEC) yielded a homogeneous species in which the Fab was a labeled with a single AuNP (Figure 2C+D), devoid of non-AuNP-labeled Fabs.
evidence: This is a primary experimental result supported by Figures 2C and 2D.

claim: Only a single Fab will bind to each PCDH15 subunit.
source: Using this reagent, we reasoned that we could directly count PCDH15 subunits because only a single Fab will bind to each PCDH15 subunit and each Fab is labeled by a single AuNP.
evidence: This is an inference based on the epitope specificity of the antibody.

claim: Each Fab is labeled by a single AuNP.
source: Using this reagent, we reasoned that we could directly count PCDH15 subunits because only a single Fab will bind to each PCDH15 subunit and each Fab is labeled by a single AuNP.
evidence: This is a property of the purified reagent as described.

claim: A complex between the 39G7 Fab – AuNP and recombinant PCDH15 was formed and isolated by SEC.
source: We confirmed this prediction by forming a complex between the 39G7 Fab – AuNP and recombinant PCDH15, isolating the complex by SEC (Figure 2E) and imaging the complex by single-particle cryo-EM (Figure 2F).
evidence: This describes an experimental validation procedure.

claim: Pairs of AuNPs bound to the PCDH15 extracellular domain were clearly identified on micrographs and tomographic reconstructions.
source: On micrographs and tomographic reconstructions (Figure 2—video 1), we clearly identified pairs of AuNPs bound to the PCDH15 extracellular domain, consistent with a dimeric model of the PCDH15 extracellular domain (Choudhary et al., 2020), the 39G7 Fab binding to EC3 and the ability of the Fab – AuNP complex to allow us to identify and count PCDH15 subunits.
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation supported by imaging data.

claim: The observation of AuNP pairs is consistent with a dimeric model of the PCDH15 extracellular domain.
source: On micrographs and tomographic reconstructions (Figure 2—video 1), we clearly identified pairs of AuNPs bound to the PCDH15 extracellular domain, consistent with a dimeric model of the PCDH15 extracellular domain (Choudhary et al., 2020), the 39G7 Fab binding to EC3 and the ability of the Fab – AuNP complex to allow us to identify and count PCDH15 subunits.
evidence: This is an inference from the imaging data supported by a citation.

claim: Cryo-EM grids were prepared using utricles stained with 39G7 Fab-AuNP.
source: We prepared cryo-EM grids using utricles stained with 39G7 Fab-AuNP and collected tomograms, primarily of stereocilia tips (Figure 3E).
evidence: This describes the experimental procedure used in the study.

claim: 3 nm gold particles were identified within ~38 nm of the stereocilia membrane on approximately half of the tomograms.
source: On approximately half of the tomograms, we identified 3 nm gold particles within ~38 nm of the stereocilia membrane, a distance that is consistent with images of the recombinant PCDH15/39G7 Fab AuNP complex (Figure 2F) and with the binding of 39G7 to EC3 of PCDH15 assuming a length of 4.5 nm per cadherin repeat (Jaiganesh et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: The distance of ~38 nm is consistent with images of the recombinant PCDH15/39G7 Fab AuNP complex.
source: On approximately half of the tomograms, we identified 3 nm gold particles within ~38 nm of the stereocilia membrane, a distance that is consistent with images of the recombinant PCDH15/39G7 Fab AuNP complex (Figure 2F) and with the binding of 39G7 to EC3 of PCDH15 assuming a length of 4.5 nm per cadherin repeat (Jaiganesh et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is an inference comparing in situ observations with in vitro data.

claim: The distance of ~38 nm is consistent with the binding of 39G7 to EC3 of PCDH15 assuming a length of 4.5 nm per cadherin repeat.
source: On approximately half of the tomograms, we identified 3 nm gold particles within ~38 nm of the stereocilia membrane, a distance that is consistent with images of the recombinant PCDH15/39G7 Fab AuNP complex (Figure 2F) and with the binding of 39G7 to EC3 of PCDH15 assuming a length of 4.5 nm per cadherin repeat (Jaiganesh et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural calculations and cited knowledge.

claim: AuNP labels were identified in tomograms of the stereocilia shaft region in about a third of the tomograms.
source: We also identified AuNP labels in tomograms of the stereocilia shaft region, but only in about a third of the tomograms that featured only stereocilia shaft regions.
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: Close inspection of the electron density around the AuNPs frequently revealed ~50 nm long filamentous density consistent with the extracellular domain of PCDH15.
source: Close inspection of the electron density around the AuNPs frequently revealed ~50 nm long filamentous density consistent with the extracellular domain of PCDH15 (Figure 3A–B, Figure 3-video 1, Figure 3-video 2).
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: In tomograms with relatively thin ice (<200 nm) and appropriate orientation, dimeric features of the PCDH15 domain are evident.
source: In tomograms with relatively thin ice (<200 nm) and an appropriate orientation of the filament to the tilt axis, dimeric features of the PCDH15 domain are evident together with AuNP pairs with a distance of 20 nm, which is consistent with two 7 nm long Fabs and an 8.5 nm helical diameter of the PCDH15 extracellular domain (Dionne et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: AuNP pairs have a distance of 20 nm.
source: In tomograms with relatively thin ice (<200 nm) and an appropriate orientation of the filament to the tilt axis, dimeric features of the PCDH15 domain are evident together with AuNP pairs with a distance of 20 nm, which is consistent with two 7 nm long Fabs and an 8.5 nm helical diameter of the PCDH15 extracellular domain (Dionne et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a measurement from tomogram analysis.

claim: The 20 nm distance between AuNP pairs is consistent with two 7 nm long Fabs and an 8.5 nm helical diameter of the PCDH15 extracellular domain.
source: In tomograms with relatively thin ice (<200 nm) and an appropriate orientation of the filament to the tilt axis, dimeric features of the PCDH15 domain are evident together with AuNP pairs with a distance of 20 nm, which is consistent with two 7 nm long Fabs and an 8.5 nm helical diameter of the PCDH15 extracellular domain (Dionne et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural measurements and cited knowledge.

claim: PCDH15 forms a dimer in stereocilia.
source: This demonstrates that PCDH15 forms a dimer in stereocilia.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation of dimeric features and AuNP pairs.

claim: Individual gold particles were observed instead of a pair of AuNPs in some cases.
source: In some cases, we observed individual gold particles instead of a pair of AuNPs (Figure 3C–D, Figure 3-video 3-4) yet also dimeric features associated with PCDH15 chain, thus indicating that the visualization of individual AuNPs was likely due to incomplete labeling of PCDH15 and not the presence of PCDH15 monomers.
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: Dimeric features were observed associated with PCDH15 chains that had only one AuNP.
source: In some cases, we observed individual gold particles instead of a pair of AuNPs (Figure 3C–D, Figure 3-video 3-4) yet also dimeric features associated with PCDH15 chain, thus indicating that the visualization of individual AuNPs was likely due to incomplete labeling of PCDH15 and not the presence of PCDH15 monomers.
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: The visualization of individual AuNPs was likely due to incomplete labeling of PCDH15 and not the presence of PCDH15 monomers.
source: In some cases, we observed individual gold particles instead of a pair of AuNPs (Figure 3C–D, Figure 3-video 3-4) yet also dimeric features associated with PCDH15 chain, thus indicating that the visualization of individual AuNPs was likely due to incomplete labeling of PCDH15 and not the presence of PCDH15 monomers.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation of dimeric features with single AuNPs.

claim: The ratio of AuNP dimers to monomers was 3:1.
source: We quantified the occurrence of AuNP dimers and monomers (Figure 3F) and found a ratio of 3:1.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of tomograms.

claim: Under the assumption that binding of the 39G7 Fab to either protomer are independent events, the fraction of PCDH15 protomers labeled with 39G7-AuNP is 0.86.
source: Under the assumption that binding of the 39G7 Fab to either protomer are independent events, we can use this ratio to estimate the fraction of PCDH15 protomers labeled with 39G7-AuNP (0.86) and the fraction of PCDH15 dimers that are completely unlabeled (0.02).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the observed ratio and statistical assumptions.

claim: Under the assumption that binding of the 39G7 Fab to either protomer are independent events, the fraction of PCDH15 dimers that are completely unlabeled is 0.02.
source: Under the assumption that binding of the 39G7 Fab to either protomer are independent events, we can use this ratio to estimate the fraction of PCDH15 protomers labeled with 39G7-AuNP (0.86) and the fraction of PCDH15 dimers that are completely unlabeled (0.02).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the observed ratio and statistical assumptions.

claim: The 39G7 Fab-AuNP robustly labels PCDH15.
source: While this may be an underestimation of the number of unlabeled PCDH15 molecules, either due to cooperativity of 39G7 binding or due to air-water interface effects, it nevertheless demonstrates that the 39G7 Fab-AuNP robustly labels PCDH15 and therefore allows precise quantification of the number of PCDH15 molecules at the tips of stereocilia.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the labeling efficiency calculations.

claim: The 39G7 Fab-AuNP allows precise quantification of the number of PCDH15 molecules at the tips of stereocilia.
source: While this may be an underestimation of the number of unlabeled PCDH15 molecules, either due to cooperativity of 39G7 binding or due to air-water interface effects, it nevertheless demonstrates that the 39G7 Fab-AuNP robustly labels PCDH15 and therefore allows precise quantification of the number of PCDH15 molecules at the tips of stereocilia.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the labeling efficiency and stoichiometry.

claim: The number of PCDH15 molecules in all imaged stereocilia tips (n=396) was carefully quantified.
source: We carefully quantified the number of PCDH15 molecules in all imaged stereocilia tips (n=396) (Figure 4F).
evidence: This describes a quantitative analysis performed in the study.

claim: 58% of stereocilia tips did not contain a PCDH15 label.
source: Slightly more than half of the stereocilia tips (58%) did not contain a PCDH15 label.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of stereocilia tips.

claim: The most likely explanation for missing PCDH15 labels is damage to stereocilia tips during the blotting of stereocilia on the cryo-EM grids.
source: While this could be due to an underestimate of the labeling efficiency or due to preferential selection of stereocilia in the tallest row, we believe the most likely explanation is damage to stereocilia tips during the blotting of stereocilia on the cryo-EM grids.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the missing labels.

claim: In 5.8% of cases, PCDH15 molecules were found in the shaft region just 'below' the stereocilia tips.
source: In some cases (5.8%), we found PCDH15 molecules in the shaft region just 'below' the stereocilia tips (Figure 4A, Figure 4-video 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of stereocilia.

claim: PCDH15 molecules found in the shaft region may have initially been located on the tip but diffused away between applying tissue to the grid and plunge-freezing.
source: It is possible that these molecules were initially located on the tip, but diffused away in the time between applying tissue to the grid and plunge-freezing.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observation.

claim: In 13% of tips, a single molecule of PCDH15 was found at the tip.
source: In 13% of tips, we found a single molecule of PCDH15 at the tip (Figure 4B+C, Figure 4-videos 2 - 3), similar to commonly depicted models of the MT complex.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of stereocilia tips.

claim: In 23% of stereocilia tips, multiple copies of PCDH15 were found at the tip.
source: However, in almost twice the number of stereocilia tips (23%), we found multiple copies of PCDH15 at the tip, either clustered at the tip (Figure 4D, Figure 4-video 4) or spread across its surface (Figure 4E, Figure 4-video 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of stereocilia tips.

claim: Multiple PCDH15 molecules at the tips may be due to stereocilia derived from immature hair cells.
source: Because we cannot determine that the maturity of the hair cells from which the stereocilia are derived, multiple PCDH15 molecules at the tips may be due to stereocilia derived from immature hair cells.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observation of multiple PCDH15 molecules.

claim: Many tips might harbor multiple copies of the MT machinery.
source: Our data, however, suggest that many tips might harbor multiple copies of the MT machinery, which in turn might underly variation in the ion channel conductance at individual tips (Beurg et al., 2018; Indzhykulian et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an inference from the observation of multiple PCDH15 molecules at tips.

claim: Multiple copies of the MT machinery might underlie variation in the ion channel conductance at individual tips.
source: Our data, however, suggest that many tips might harbor multiple copies of the MT machinery, which in turn might underly variation in the ion channel conductance at individual tips (Beurg et al., 2018; Indzhykulian et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations to relevant literature.

claim: Electron-density extending beyond the tip of PCDH15, consistent with a 120 nm long filament inserted into two distinct membranes, was found in a few tomograms.
source: In a few tomograms, we found electron-density extending beyond the tip of PCDH15, consistent with a 120 nm long filament inserted into two distinct membranes (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: The density extending beyond PCDH15 is speculated to correspond to CDH23.
source: While we cannot determine the molecular identity of this density unambiguously, based on the dimensions of this molecule, we speculate that the density corresponds to CDH23.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the dimensions of the observed density.

claim: A stereocilium tip with five copies of a PCDH15 dimer was found, three of which were connected to a possible CDH23 density inserted into a small spherical liposome.
source: In one example, we found a stereocilium tip with five copies of a PCDH15 dimer, three of which were connected to a possible CDH23 density, which in turn was inserted into a small spherical liposome (Figure 5A, Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: The structure with PCDH15 connected to CDH23 in a liposome may be a tip link assembly disrupted during sample preparation.
source: Our interpretation of this structure is that it may be a tip link assembly, disrupted during sample preparation, where a portion of the membrane surrounding CDH23 was 'torn off' of the neighboring stereocilium, yielding CDH23 bound to a liposome.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed structure.

claim: A cluster of five PCDH15 molecules close to a stereocilium tip is connected to four possible CDH23 densities inserted into a lipid membrane fragment.
source: In another case, a cluster of five PCDH15 molecules close to a stereocilium tip is connected to four possible CDH23 densities inserted into a lipid membrane fragment (Figure 5B, Figure 5—video 2).
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: Structures were observed in which PCDH15, together with a fraction of surrounding membrane, appears to have been extracted from the shorter stereocilium.
source: We also observed structures in which it appears as though PCDH15, together with a fraction of surrounding membrane, was extracted from the shorter stereocilium (Figure 5C + D, Figure 5—videos 3-4).
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: In structures where PCDH15 appears extracted, 3–5 copies of PCDH15 and, putatively, CDH23 were found.
source: In both cases, we found 3–5 copies of PCDH15 and, putatively, CDH23.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: Most PCDH15 complexes were observed in structures that appear to be the result of partial damage of the tip link.
source: The fact that we observed most PCDH15 complexes in structures that appear to be the result of partial damage of the tip link is consistent with the earlier interpretation of the missing PCDH15 label is due to damaged tip links.
evidence: This is an inference from the pattern of observations.

claim: Clusters of PCDH15 complexes may be more stable than single PCDH15 complexes.
source: It is also possible that clusters of PCDH15 complexes are more stable than single PCDH15 complexes, and thus more frequently observed.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observation patterns.

claim: A tomogram was obtained showing the tip of a stereocilium situated next to a longer stereocilium with 17 AuNPs at the tip of the shorter stereocilium.
source: In one tomogram, we imaged the tip of a stereocilium situated next to a longer stereocilium (Figure 6A, Figure 6-video 1). While we observed 17 AuNPs at the tip of the shorter stereocilium, we only unambiguously identified the density for four PCDH15 molecules.
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: Only four PCDH15 molecules were unambiguously identified despite 17 AuNPs being observed.
source: In one tomogram, we imaged the tip of a stereocilium situated next to a longer stereocilium (Figure 6A, Figure 6-video 1). While we observed 17 AuNPs at the tip of the shorter stereocilium, we only unambiguously identified the density for four PCDH15 molecules.
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: A 120 nm long filament was observed connecting one PCDH15 molecule to the longer stereocilium.
source: On one of these PCDH15 molecules, we observed a 120 nm long filament, connecting PCDH15 to the longer stereocilium (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: The 120 nm long filament connecting PCDH15 to the longer stereocilium is hypothesized to be an intact tip link.
source: We hypothesize that this is most likely an intact tip link.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed structure.

claim: Dimeric features can be clearly identified on the PCDH15 molecule in the putative intact tip link.
source: Upon closer inspection (Figure 6C), we can clearly identify dimeric features on this PCDH15 molecule.
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from detailed tomogram analysis.

claim: Other adjacent PCDH15 molecules are clearly dimeric entities but are not bound to a potential CDH23 partner.
source: Other adjacent PCDH15 molecules are also clearly dimeric entities (Figure 6D), yet are not bound to a potential CDH23 partner.
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: Another copy of PCDH15 was identified further down the two stereocilia, apparently connected via a potential CDH23 molecule to the other stereocilium.
source: Further down the two stereocilia, we identified another copy of PCDH15, apparently connected via a potential CDH23 molecule to the other stereocilium (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: PCDH15 appears to be bent by about 90° near the juncture of the EC9-EC10 cadherin domains in one observed structure.
source: In this case, PCDH15 appears to be bent, by about 90o, near the juncture of the EC9-EC10 cadherin domains, a 'joint' between cadherin domains that has previously been identified as flexible in cryo-EM and crystallography structures of PCDH15 extracellular domain constructs (Araya-Secchi et al., 2016; Ge et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: The EC9-EC10 interface has previously been identified as flexible in cryo-EM and crystallography structures of PCDH15 extracellular domain constructs.
source: In this case, PCDH15 appears to be bent, by about 90o, near the juncture of the EC9-EC10 cadherin domains, a 'joint' between cadherin domains that has previously been identified as flexible in cryo-EM and crystallography structures of PCDH15 extracellular domain constructs (Araya-Secchi et al., 2016; Ge et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The bent PCDH15-CDH23 link may be in the process of being trafficked to the tip.
source: We speculate that this link may be in the process of being trafficked to the tip and that the EC9-EC10 bend helps to accommodate the long filament within the relatively narrow space between stereocilia.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed bent structure.

claim: The EC9-EC10 bend may help to accommodate the long filament within the relatively narrow space between stereocilia.
source: We speculate that this link may be in the process of being trafficked to the tip and that the EC9-EC10 bend helps to accommodate the long filament within the relatively narrow space between stereocilia.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the functional significance of the bend.

claim: Several tomograms exhibit numbers of labels consistent with hundreds of copies of PCDH15.
source: While in the majority of tomograms, we identified 10 or fewer copies of PCDH15, several tomograms exhibit numbers of labels consistent with hundreds of copies of PCDH15.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from tomogram analysis.

claim: Labels were observed between stereocilia that appear thinner and less densely packed with actin than other stereocilia.
source: In the most striking example (Figure 7A, Figure 7-video 1), we observed these labels between stereocilia that appear thinner and less densely packed with actin than other stereocilia.

claim: 309 AuNPs were counted in one tomogram showing extensive lateral links.
source: In this tomogram, we counted 309 AuNPs and modeled 56 PCDH15 molecules in cases where we observed the corresponding electron density.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from tomogram analysis.

claim: 56 PCDH15 molecules were modeled in the tomogram showing extensive lateral links.
source: In this tomogram, we counted 309 AuNPs and modeled 56 PCDH15 molecules in cases where we observed the corresponding electron density.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from tomogram analysis.

claim: Many of the PCDH15 molecules are involved in links to neighboring stereocilia via a 120 nm filament.
source: Many of the PCDH15 molecules are involved in links to neighboring stereocilia, via a 120 nm filament, which again may be a CDH23 molecule.
evidence: This is a primary experimental observation from tomogram analysis.

source: We observed density for 20 putative CDH23 molecules, molecules that likely participate in the 'lateral links' which form early in development of stereocilia bundles and are composed of PCDH15 and CDH23 (Michel et al., 2005).

claim: Lateral links form early in development of stereocilia bundles and are composed of PCDH15 and CDH23.
source: We observed density for 20 putative CDH23 molecules, molecules that likely participate in the 'lateral links' which form early in development of stereocilia bundles and are composed of PCDH15 and CDH23 (Michel et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Multiple copies of the potential CDH23 molecules cluster together, primarily via their N-terminal half.
source: Inspection of the densities shows that multiple copies of the potential CDH23 molecules cluster together, primarily via their N-terminal half so as to obscure identification of individual stands (Figure 7B+C).

claim: Clustering of CDH23 molecules obscures identification of individual strands.
source: Inspection of the densities shows that multiple copies of the potential CDH23 molecules cluster together, primarily via their N-terminal half so as to obscure identification of individual stands (Figure 7B+C).

source: We speculate that these clusters might have given rise to the appearance of single tip links with multiple upper and lower insertion points in stained EM images.

claim: Examples of putative CDH23 molecules that appear bent halfway between the N- and C-termini were found.
source: Furthermore, we find examples of putative CDH23 molecules that appear bent halfway between the N- and C-termini, indicating that CDH23 might also have a flexible cadherin domain 'joint,' similar to the EC9-EC10 interface of PCDH15 (Figure 7D).
